mainTopic: Whether the יבם, as heir of the כתובה, must bury a שומרת יבם, and whether a יבמה's כתובה can count as collectible while she is bound to the יבם.
overview: This amud asks who must pay to bury a שומרת יבם, a widow waiting for יבום. The rule is that the heirs of her כתובה bury her. אביי supports this from a משנה that speaks of a widow with two sets of heirs, which can only be a שומרת יבם. רבא asks why the יבם can't say, 'I inherit my brother, but burying his wife is not my job.' אביי answers that he is pressed from two sides: either bury her or pay her כתובה. רבא replies that a כתובה is not collected during the husband's lifetime, and the יבם stands in for the husband. The גמרא argues that this idea comes from בית שמאי, who also hold that a document ready to be collected counts as already collected, and proves it from the משנה about a סוטה whose husband died. The גמרא then cites the plain wording 'when you marry another', and רב אשי answers that the יבם also counts as 'another man.' Finally רבא sends אביי a new challenge from סומכוס's teaching: a יבם who wants to sell his brother's property must make a feast to win his wife over, or divorce her and remarry her.

steps.title: The heirs of her כתובה must bury her
steps.stepSummary: The ruling ends: whoever inherits a woman's כתובה must pay for her burial.
steps.simpleTranslation: Her heirs, the heirs of her כתובה, are obligated to bury her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes stating a rule: the people who inherit a woman's כתובה must take care of her burial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burial is tied to the money of the כתובה. Whoever ends up with the כתובה money also takes on the cost of burying her.

keyTerms.meaning: The heirs of her כתובה, the people who end up with her marriage-contract money
Burial
They are obligated

phrases.english: Her heirs, the heirs of her marriage contract,
are obligated in her burial.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ruling that came just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever inherits the woman's כתובה must pay for her burial.

steps.title: אביי brings support from a משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a משנה that has the same wording: a widow is supported by the orphans, but the heirs of her כתובה bury her.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We also learned this in a משנה: A widow is fed from the orphans' property, her earnings belong to them, and they are not obligated to bury her. Her heirs, the heirs of her כתובה, are obligated to bury her.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי says, 'We already have a משנה that teaches this,' and quotes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the orphans feed the widow and keep her earnings, but they do not bury her. Instead, 'her heirs, the heirs of her כתובה' bury her. That is the same phrase as our ruling, and the next steps show which widow it means.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it (in a משנה): a formula for bringing support
She is fed and supported
Her earnings, what she makes from her work
Orphans, the husband's children and heirs

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא:
phrases.english: Abaye said: We too have learned:
A widow is supported from the property of the orphans,
and her earnings are theirs,
and they are not obligated in her burial.
Her heirs, the heirs of her marriage contract,
are obligated in her burial.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה to support the ruling in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the heirs of the כתובה must bury her.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: 'A widow is supported from the property of the orphans'.

steps.title: Which widow has two sets of heirs?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks which widow could have two different sets of heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: And which widow has two sets of heirs?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks a question that sets up the next move: what kind of widow does the משנה mean?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's wording, 'her heirs, the heirs of her כתובה,' suggests two different groups of heirs. Normally a widow's heirs are just her own family, so אביי asks who this widow could be.

keyTerms.meaning: Two sets of heirs
Which one is it?

phrases.english: And which is the widow
that has two sets of heirs?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵיזוֹהִי אַלְמָנָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ שְׁנֵי יוֹרְשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the wording of the משנה quoted in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which widow has separate heirs for her own property and for her כתובה?

steps.title: It must be a שומרת יבם
steps.stepSummary: The only widow who fits is a שומרת יבם, so the משנה matches our ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: You must say: this is a שומרת יבם.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers his own question: the משנה must be talking about a widow waiting for יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a שומרת יבם, the יבם is the one who would inherit her כתובה, while her own relatives inherit her other belongings. That is why the משנה separates 'her heirs' from 'the heirs of her כתובה,' and it proves that the יבם must bury her.

keyTerms.meaning: You must say: this is the only possible answer
A widow waiting for her late husband's brother to do יבום or חליצה

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's 'heirs of her כתובה' refers to the יבם, so he must pay for the burial of a שומרת יבם.

phrases.english: You must say: this is a widow waiting for her yavam.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3 and completes אביי's proof.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The widow with two sets of heirs is a שומרת יבם, and the יבם is the heir of her כתובה.

steps.title: רבא: Let the יבם refuse to bury her
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks why the יבם can't say he inherits his brother but has no duty to bury his brother's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Let him say, 'I inherit my brother. His wife I don't bury.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges the ruling by suggesting an argument the יבם could make to get out of paying for the burial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יבם gets the money because he is his brother's heir. רבא asks why that should make him responsible for the wife, since inheriting the brother doesn't obviously mean taking on the wife's burial.

keyTerms.meaning: But let him say
I inherit my brother
Buries

phrases.english: Rava said: But let him say:
I inherit my brother.
His wife I do not bury.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling that אביי just supported.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the יבם, as heir of the כתובה, must bury her.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Inheriting the brother's estate doesn't automatically mean inheriting a duty toward the brother's wife.

steps.title: אביי: He is pressed from two sides
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the יבם is stuck either way: if he is the heir he must bury her, and if he won't bury her he must pay her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Because they come at him from two sides. If he inherits his brother, let him bury his brother's wife. If he does not bury his brother's wife, let him give her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רבא's challenge by showing that the יבם has no way out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the יבם acts as his brother's heir, he takes on his brother's duty to bury his wife. If he refuses that role, then the כתובה is owed and must be paid out of the estate, so he loses the money anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: They come at him, they make a claim against him
From two sides
He must pay her כתובה

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Because they come at him from two sides:

phrases.aramaic: אִם אָחִיו יוֹרֵשׁ — יִקְבּוֹר אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ.
phrases.english: If he inherits his brother, let him bury his wife.
phrases.notes: 'His wife' means the dead brother's wife, the שומרת יבם.

phrases.aramaic: אִם אֵינוֹ קוֹבֵר אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ — יִתֵּן כְּתוּבָּתָהּ.
phrases.english: If he does not bury his wife, let him give her marriage contract.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: מִשּׁוּם דְּבָאִין עָלָיו מִשְּׁנֵי צְדָדִין
steps.terutzResolutionType: A two-sided argument: either choice leads to an obligation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The יבם can take the inheritance and ignore the wife.
steps.terutzMaskana: He must either bury her as the heir or pay her כתובה.

steps.title: רבא: A כתובה can't be collected while the husband is alive
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the יבם doesn't owe the כתובה either, because a כתובה is not collected 'during the husband's lifetime', and the יבם stands in for the husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what I mean. 'I inherit my brother, and his wife I don't bury.' And if you say he must pay the כתובה, a כתובה is not given to be collected during the husband's lifetime.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on אביי's answer by removing the second 'side': the יבם doesn't have to pay the כתובה now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As long as the woman is waiting for יבום, the יבם stands in the dead husband's place. A כתובה is only paid when the marriage ends, not while there is still a 'husband'. So the יבם can say he owes neither burial nor כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what I am saying: a clarification of one's own point
A כתובה is not meant to be collected while the husband is alive

steps.confusionAlert: רבא isn't saying the dead brother is alive. He means the יבם fills the husband's role, so the כתובה is not yet due.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what I am saying:
I inherit my brother,
his wife I do not bury.
And if it is because of the marriage contract,
a marriage contract was not given to be collected during life.
phrases.notes: He means during the husband's life. The יבם counts as the husband here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the second 'side' of אביי's answer in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the יבם must pay the כתובה if he won't bury her.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A כתובה isn't collected while the husband, or his stand-in the יבם, is still in place.

steps.title: That idea comes from בית שמאי, who also say a ready document counts as collected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: the idea of reading the כתובה's wording comes from בית שמאי, and they also hold that a document ready to be collected counts as already collected.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whom have you heard who expounds the wording of the כתובה? בית שמאי. And we have heard בית שמאי say: a document that stands to be collected is considered as if collected!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's reasoning by showing that its source, בית שמאי, holds another rule that works against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'no collecting during the husband's life' comes from reading the exact words of the כתובה, which is בית שמאי's approach. But בית שמאי also say a document ready to be collected counts as already collected. So the כתובה should count as hers already, and רבא's way out for the יבם doesn't work.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning rules from the exact wording of the כתובה
The students of שמאי
A document that stands ready to be collected
It is considered as if already collected

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a source's own other rulings can undo an argument built on it. You can't borrow one idea from בית שמאי and ignore their related rule.

phrases.english: Whom have you heard
who holds that one expounds the marriage contract?
Beit Shammai.
And we have heard Beit Shammai, who say:
A document that stands to be collected
is considered as if collected!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ דְּאִית לֵיהּ מִדְרַשׁ כְּתוּבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source of רבא's argument in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the כתובה cannot be collected during the 'husband's' life.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source of that rule, בית שמאי, also holds that a ready-to-collect document counts as collected, so the כתובה counts as hers already.

steps.title: The משנה about a suspected wife whose husband died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: if husbands died before their suspected wives drank the bitter waters, בית שמאי say the wives collect their כתובה and do not drink. בית הלל say they either drink or do not collect.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: If the husbands died before the wives drank, בית שמאי say: They take the כתובה and do not drink. בית הלל say: Either they drink or they do not take the כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to back up its claim from step 8 about what בית שמאי hold. This sets up the next few moves, which will read the משנה closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a wife suspected of being unfaithful (a סוטה), whose husband died before the test of the bitter waters. Nobody knows if she sinned. בית שמאי still let her collect her כתובה, and that ruling will be the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: A wife suspected of being unfaithful, who is tested with the bitter waters
They drink (the bitter waters of a סוטה)
They take (collect) their כתובה money

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: מֵתוּ בַּעֲלֵיהֶן עַד שֶׁלֹּא שָׁתוּ —
phrases.english: As we learned: If their husbands died before they drank,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in סוטה 24a about suspected wives who never got to drink the bitter waters.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:
They take the marriage contract and do not drink,
And Beit Hillel say:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שׁוֹתוֹת אוֹ לֹא נוֹטְלוֹת כְּתוּבָה.
phrases.english: Either they drink or they do not take the marriage contract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for step 8's claim about בית שמאי.
steps.raayaObject: That בית שמאי hold a document ready to be collected counts as already collected
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in סוטה about wives whose husbands died before they drank

steps.title: How can a widow drink the bitter waters?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is puzzled by בית הלל's words 'either they drink': the תורה requires the husband to bring his wife to the כהן, and here there is no husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Either they drink'?! The תורה says: 'Then the man shall bring his wife to the כהן', and here there is no husband!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to challenge the wording of בית הלל's view in the משנה. A woman whose husband died cannot drink the bitter waters at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק makes the husband part of the process: he brings his wife to the כהן. Once he is dead, the test can never happen. So the option 'either they drink' makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
And there is none (here, no husband)

phrases.english: Either they drink?!
"Then the man shall bring his wife to the priest"
the Merciful One said, and there is none!
phrases.notes: He means there is no husband anymore to bring her, since he died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of בית הלל's view in the quoted משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק requires the husband to bring her, so a widow can never drink.

steps.title: Reading בית הלל correctly: since she can't drink, she doesn't collect
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads בית הלל: since these women cannot drink, they cannot collect their כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means: since they do not drink, they do not take the כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading of בית הלל's words. They are not offering a choice. They mean that because she can't drink, she loses her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Drinking was the only way to clear her name. With the husband dead, she can't prove she did nothing wrong. So according to בית הלל she cannot collect.

keyTerms.meaning: Since / because

phrases.english: Rather: since they do not drink,
they do not take the marriage contract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by rereading בית הלל's words.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית הלל give a choice: drink or give up the כתובה
steps.terutzMaskana: בית הלל mean: since she cannot drink, she cannot collect

steps.title: Why do בית שמאי let a doubtful claim win?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to בית שמאי's view and asks: maybe she sinned and maybe not. How can her doubtful claim take money away from the heirs, who are certain owners?
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: They take the כתובה and do not drink. But why? It is a doubt: maybe she was unfaithful, maybe she was not. And a doubtful claim comes and takes money away from a certain claim!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to בית שמאי's ruling and questions it. This sets up the key answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally money stays with whoever holds it unless a clear claim takes it away. The heirs surely own their father's property. The wife's right to the כתובה is only a ספק, so by normal rules she should lose.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt, an uncertain case
She was unfaithful
A doubtful claim takes away from a certain one, which normally does not happen

steps.confusionAlert: The 'certain' side here is the heirs, not the wife. They surely inherit their father's property, while her right to the כתובה is in doubt.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:
They take the marriage contract and do not drink.
But why? It is a doubt:
maybe she was unfaithful, maybe she was not unfaithful,
and a doubt comes and takes out of the hands of a certainty!
phrases.notes: The 'certainty' is the heirs, who surely own their father's property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side point about בית הלל and returns to בית שמאי's ruling, the actual proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's ruling that the widow collects her כתובה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Her right is only a ספק, and a ספק should not take money from the heirs, who are certain owners.

steps.title: בית שמאי: a document ready to be collected counts as collected
steps.stepSummary: The answer: בית שמאי hold that a document ready to be collected is treated as if it were already collected. So the כתובה money already counts as the wife's.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי hold: A document that is ready to be collected is considered already collected.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains בית שמאי's ruling. This also proves the claim made in step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If her כתובה already counts as collected, the money is in her hands. Now the heirs are the ones with the doubtful claim trying to take money from her. So she keeps it.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold / it is their view
A document that is ready to be collected
Is considered as already collected

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי hold שטר העומד לגבות כגבוי דמי. This is the proof for step 8's challenge to רבא: the same בית שמאי who read the כתובה's wording also treat a כתובה as already collected.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle turns the situation around. The person holding the document counts as already holding the money, so the other side must prove its claim.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai hold:
A document that is ready to be collected is considered collected.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 and completes the proof begun in step 9 for step 8's claim.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing to the underlying principle behind the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Her claim is a doubtful one trying to take money from the certain heirs
steps.terutzMaskana: Her כתובה already counts as collected, so the money is treated as hers

steps.title: The Contract Only Pays When She Marries Someone Else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the כתובה document says 'when you marry another, you will take what is written for you.' The יבמה has not married anyone else, so how can she claim it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But don't we need the wording 'When you marry another, you may take what is written for you'? That isn't happening here!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that the יבמה can have a claim to her כתובה right now. It points to the plain wording of the כתובה document itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כתובה promises payment 'when you marry another,' meaning once the marriage has ended and she moves on. A יבמה tied to the יבם cannot marry anyone else before חליצה. So by the document's own words, her right to collect has not started yet.

keyTerms.meaning: But don't we require…? (opens a challenge)
When you marry another man (a line in the כתובה)
You will take what is written for you
And it is not there / that isn't the case

phrases.english: But don't we require:
"When you marry another man
you may take what is written for you,"
and that is not the case here?
phrases.notes: She is still bound to the יבם and can't marry anyone else yet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on steps 8 and 13. Even without בית שמאי's מדרש כתובה, the plain words of the כתובה ('when you marry another') stop her from collecting while she is bound to the יבם. So treating the כתובה as already collected does not help.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the יבמה has a present claim to her כתובה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כתובה's own wording makes payment depend on her marrying another man, which a יבמה bound to the יבם has not done.

steps.title: The יבם Counts as 'Another Man'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the יבם is also considered 'another man,' so the condition in the כתובה is fulfilled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: A יבם is also treated like 'another man.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge. Being married to the יבם counts as 'marrying another.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'another man' do not have to mean a stranger. Anyone other than her first husband counts, and the יבם is a different man from the brother who died. So the condition written in the כתובה has been met.

keyTerms.meaning: The brother of the man who died childless, who marries his widow
Is treated like another man

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
A yavam is also considered like another man.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: יָבָם נָמֵי כְּאַחֵר דָּמֵי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefinition of a term in the document
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Another man' means someone outside the family, so the יבמה has not met the condition.
steps.terutzMaskana: The יבם counts as 'another man,' so the condition is fulfilled.

steps.title: רבא Asks: Can a כתובה Be Collected During the Marriage?
steps.stepSummary: רבא sends a question to אביי through a messenger: is a כתובה ever meant to be collected while the marriage is still going on?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא sent this to אביי through רב שמעיה בר זירא: Can a כתובה really be collected while he is alive?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a new challenge to the whole idea. He doubts that a כתובה can be paid out while she is still married to him. The ברייתא he uses as proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the יבם counts as 'another man,' she is still married to him right now. A כתובה is meant to be paid when the marriage ends, by death or divorce. So how can she have any claim to it during the marriage?

keyTerms.meaning: He sent to him (a message)
Through, by way of (a messenger)
To be collected during the husband's lifetime

phrases.english: Rava sent to Abaye
by way of Rav Shemaya bar Zeira:
And was a ketubah ever given
to be collected during his lifetime?
phrases.notes: He means while the יבם is alive and still married to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רָבָא לְאַבָּיֵי בְּיַד רַב שְׁמַעְיָה בַּר זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge from רבא, aimed at whether a כתובה can be paid during the marriage at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the יבמה has a present claim to her כתובה while married to the יבם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כתובה is paid only when the marriage ends, not while it is still going on.

steps.title: Sumakhos: Persuade Her or Divorce Her
steps.stepSummary: רבא supports his challenge with a ברייתא. סומכוס taught that a יבם who wants to sell his dead brother's property must either win his wife over at a feast (if he is a כהן) or divorce her and remarry her (if he is a ישראל).
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אבא says, I asked סומכוס: If someone wants to sell his brother's property, what should he do? If he is a כהן, he should make a feast and win her over. If he is a ישראל, he should divorce her with a גט and then take her back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a ברייתא as proof for his question. It shows that a יבם cannot simply pay off his wife's כתובה during the marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dead brother's property is tied up to back the יבמה's כתובה, so the יבם cannot sell it freely. If a כתובה could be paid during the marriage, סומכוס would just tell him to pay her and free the property. Instead he offers only two roundabout options: win her agreement, or end the marriage with a גט. That suggests a כתובה is not collected while the marriage lasts.

keyTerms.meaning: His brother's property
And he should win her over / persuade her
He divorces her with a גט and then takes her back

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי: the יבם counts as 'another man' for the wording of the כתובה. But רבא challenges whether a כתובה can be collected during the marriage at all, and proves it from סומכוס's advice: a feast or a divorce, never simply paying her off.
steps.confusionAlert: The divorce is not a real break-up. It is a temporary step so the property is freed from the כתובה, and then he remarries her. A כהן cannot do this, because a כהן may not marry a divorced woman, even his own ex-wife.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: Rabbi Abba says,
I asked Sumakhos:
One who wants to sell his brother's property,
phrases.notes: This is the יבם selling his dead brother's property, which is tied up to back the יבמה's כתובה.

phrases.english: how should he go about it?
If he is a priest —
he should make a feast and win her over.
If he is an Israelite —
he divorces her with a get and takes her back.
phrases.notes: After the divorce he pays only her כתובה, sells the rest, and then remarries her.
